designSummary: Comparison of mean clinic cost per episode between two consecutive periods, with bootstrap intervals; consequences as proportions; budget impact as a deterministic model with scenarios.
sampleSize: About 950 episodes per period. With a standard deviation of clinic cost per episode of about 40 (a planning value; the observed value replaces it), the 95 percent interval for the difference in means has a half-width of about 3.6 (40 times the square root of 2/950, times 1.96), small enough to show whether 14 minutes of set-up time for each new app user is offset by 6 shorter minutes per appointment with a usable diary. Usable diaries near 67 percent give an interval of about plus or minus 4.2 points per period.
primaryAnalysis: Difference in mean clinic cost per episode with a bootstrap interval from 2,000 resamples; costs at 2026 staff rates.
secondaryAnalysis: Usable diaries and time to eligibility decision by period; usable diaries for patients aged 70 or over by diary type; three-year budget impact for injectable preventives under three eligibility scenarios (observed change, half of it, and the 18 percent projection), at 4,900 per treated patient per year (claim c4).
missingData: Appointments without booking times are excluded from time costs and counted; missing set-up logs are imputed with the monthly median and flagged.
multiplicity: One primary comparison; secondary outcomes and scenarios reported descriptively.
software: R; the budget impact model in a documented spreadsheet.
overfittingGuards: Cost items and staff rates fixed before the switch
No subgroup beyond age 70 or over
summary: About 950 episodes per period give a half-width of about 3.6 for the cost difference; budget impact by scenario.
